name: re-entrant-loft
why: A re-entrant loft section, allowed since sections no longer need to be convex: a ruled loft between an L and the L at half size is the frustum h/3 (A1 + A2 + sqrt(A1 A2)) = 5250 mm3 exactly, every wall planar. A pairing that slipped one vertex would twist the walls into saddles and read short: the twisted-loft tripwire applied to a non-convex outline. The mesher's triangle count is held to 260%: BRepMesh's deflection control asks to insert the midpoint of each planar wall's diagonal, a point exactly on the link it would split, and whether the Delaunay insertion takes it is a rounding tie. Native arm64 drops it and leaves five walls two triangles each (634); the WebAssembly build takes it and refines them to a few hundred (2240). Volume, area, size and topology agree to every recorded digit, which is what this case holds; see docs/GOTCHAS.md, "A planar wall meshes two ways".
